quality_analysis.test_quality_notes: No tests around Stripe webhook handling or payment intent creation despite being the most critical/financial path.

findings.description: server/src/controllers/payment.controller.js:26-32 - Payment.create() is called without a subscriptionId, but getPaymentHistory (line 103-105) later joins payments to subscriptions via payment.subscriptionId, which is never set anywhere in this file.
findings.suggestion: Set subscriptionId on the Payment record once the subscription is created/activated after payment success.

findings.description: server/src/controllers/payment.controller.js:56-66 - Stripe webhook handler has no idempotency/duplicate-event check, so a retried webhook delivery (Stripe retries on non-2xx) can reprocess the same payment_intent.succeeded event.
findings.suggestion: Record processed Stripe event IDs and skip already-handled events.

findings.description: server/src/controllers/payment.controller.js:111-122 - getPaymentHistory maps over payments and calls subscriptions.find(...) inside the loop (Array.find per payment), an O(n*m) scan instead of building a lookup map first.
findings.suggestion: Build a Map keyed by subscription._id before mapping payments.

findings.description: server/src/index.js:53-58 - connectDB().then(...) has no .catch; a failed MongoDB connection produces an unhandled promise rejection instead of a logged/graceful shutdown.
findings.suggestion: Add a .catch(err => { console.error(err); process.exit(1); }) after the .then() chain.

findings.description: server/src/index.js - no rate-limiting middleware (e.g. express-rate-limit) is applied to any route, including public /api/auth endpoints.
findings.suggestion: Add express-rate-limit or push rate limiting to an API gateway/reverse proxy.

name: Repository Architecture
summary:
This repository implements a gym subscription management application split into a `client` (React 18 + Vite + Tailwind SPA) and a `server` (Node.js/Express REST API). The backend exposes auth, user, subscription-plan, subscription, and payment endpoints backed by MongoDB via Mongoose models. All top-level project documentation (README.md, SETUP_INSTRUCTIONS.md, QUICK_START.md, PROJECT_STRUCTURE.md, MIGRATION_COMPLETE.md, server/MONGODB_MIGRATION.md) has been removed from the repository, leaving only build/runtime configuration files to describe how the project is set up.

The backend follows a conventional Express layered structure: routes -> controllers -> Mongoose models, with shared middleware for JWT auth, request validation, and centralized error handling. Payments are the most complex module, integrating the Stripe SDK to create PaymentIntents and to verify/handle asynchronous Stripe webhook events (payment_intent.succeeded / payment_intent.payment_failed).

The frontend is a client-rendered SPA using React Router for navigation, a Context-based AuthContext for session/JWT state, and an Axios wrapper (services/api.js) as the single point of contact with the backend REST API. Route protection is implemented client-side via a ProtectedRoute component gating page access based on AuthContext state.

Testing is minimal: only the auth controller has a Jest test file, and there is no frontend test setup at all. The most business-critical and highest-risk code path (Stripe webhook handling and payment/subscription linkage) is entirely untested.

text: This repository implements a gym subscription management application split into a `client` (React 18 + Vite + Tailwind SPA) and a `server` (Node.js/Express REST API). The backend exposes auth, user, subscription-plan, subscription, and payment endpoints backed by MongoDB via Mongoose models. All top-level project documentation (README.md, SETUP_INSTRUCTIONS.md, QUICK_START.md, PROJECT_STRUCTURE.md, MIGRATION_COMPLETE.md, server/MONGODB_MIGRATION.md) has been removed from the repository, leaving only build/runtime configuration files to describe how the project is set up.

The backend follows a conventional Express layered structure: routes -> controllers -> Mongoose models, with shared middleware for JWT auth, request validation, and centralized error handling. Payments are the most complex module, integrating the Stripe SDK to create PaymentIntents and to verify/handle asynchronous Stripe webhook events (payment_intent.succeeded / payment_intent.payment_failed).

The frontend is a client-rendered SPA using React Router for navigation, a Context-based AuthContext for session/JWT state, and an Axios wrapper (services/api.js) as the single point of contact with the backend REST API. Route protection is implemented client-side via a ProtectedRoute component gating page access based on AuthContext state.

Testing is minimal: only the auth controller has a Jest test file, and there is no frontend test setup at all. The most business-critical and highest-risk code path (Stripe webhook handling and payment/subscription linkage) is entirely untested.

pros: Clear, conventional separation between routes, controllers, and models on the backend, and between pages, components, and services on the frontend.
Payment amounts are computed server-side from the stored plan price rather than trusting client input, avoiding a common price-tampering vulnerability.
Stripe webhook signature verification is implemented (constructEvent with the webhook secret) before processing any webhook event.
Raw-body middleware is correctly scoped only to the /api/payments/webhook route while the rest of the API uses standard JSON parsing.
Centralized error-handling middleware and a dedicated auth middleware give consistent cross-cutting behavior across route modules.
cons: createPaymentIntent never sets subscriptionId on the created Payment record, so getPaymentHistory's join between payments and subscriptions is effectively broken for new payments.
connectDB().then(...) in server/src/index.js has no .catch, so a MongoDB connection failure causes an unhandled promise rejection instead of a controlled failure/exit.
No idempotency handling on the Stripe webhook handler, leaving it exposed to duplicate-event reprocessing on Stripe's automatic retries.
Test coverage is limited to a single auth test file; the payments/subscriptions logic and the entire frontend have zero automated tests.
All project-level documentation (README, setup/quick-start guides, project structure, migration notes) was deleted, leaving new contributors without any written onboarding or API reference material.
No rate limiting on any endpoint, including public authentication routes, leaving login/register open to brute-force attempts.

dataflow.name: User Registration & Login
dataflow.description: Frontend Register/Login pages call the [[Auth]] Module via the Axios client; the [[Auth]] Module validates credentials against the [[User]] Module's MongoDB-backed [[User]] model and issues a JWT stored in AuthContext.

dataflow.name: Subscription Purchase & Payment
dataflow.description: Member selects a plan on the [[Plans]] page; the [[Payments]] Module fetches the plan price, creates a [[Stripe]] PaymentIntent, and [[Stripe]] later delivers a webhook that updates payment status and (intendedly) the linked Subscription.

dataflow.name: Server Bootstrap
dataflow.description: index.js loads env config, connects to MongoDB, wires middleware and route modules, and starts the Express server.

dataflow.name: Payment History View
dataflow.description: The MySubscription page requests payment history through the API client; the [[Payments]] Module reads Payment records and joins them with Subscription/Plan data before returning the response.
